title: wave-synchronizer-and-provenance-backed-resume-controller
author: Marcus Alvarez
release_notes: Adds a wave synchronizer that coordinates cross-cohort rollbacks and a provenance-backed resume controller that validates signal attribution before resuming traffic. Includes deterministic replay tooling and console controls for manual overrides.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed incidents where rolling back one cohort caused unexpected regressions in dependent cohorts because telemetry attribution was ambiguous and resume decisions lacked provenance checks. This PR implements a wave synchronizer service to coordinate multi-cohort state transitions and a provenance-backed resume controller that enforces gating checks before allowing waves to advance or resume.

Key changes:
- Wave synchronizer service: maintains per-rollout directed dependency graphs (wave->depends_on waves), enforces safe ordering, and serializes decision application to prevent flip-flops.
- Provenance tagging: routing layer emits compact provenance tokens (sample_id|rollout|wave|variant) for sampled requests. Ingestion sidecar decodes tokens and attributes metrics to the originating wave.
- Resume controller: evaluates aggregated telemetry per-wave (latency p95, error rate, semantic drift samples) over configured windows and applies a three-step gating (smoke, stability, long-term quality) before allowing resume.
- Replay harness: sampled request blobs and model snapshot pointers are stored in compressed blobs for deterministic replay in investigation mode; admin console exposes replay controls.
- Safe defaults and opt-in automation: default behavior is 'recommend' mode. Auto-execute rollbacks/resumes require an account-level opt-in and RBAC permission.

Implementation notes:
- Data model: rollout records now include a provenance_index field used by the telemetry pipeline. Migration added a compact index table to keep lookup cheap.
- Token format: compact pipe-delimited ASCII to avoid base64 overhead on hot paths; tokens are optionally HMAC-signed for private deployments.
- Decision idempotency: decisions are tagged with a monotonic decision_nonce and stored with the wave state to prevent repeated toggles. A flip-flop detector raises an alert after two state reversals within a cooldown window.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for synchronizer state machine and resume gating logic.
- Integration test that wires synchronizer, routing sampler, and telemetry adaptor in a local cluster.
- Staging run with three internal canaries for 48h to validate attribution and gating thresholds.

Files changed (high level):
- services/wave-synchronizer/ (new): orchestrator and state machine
- routing/sampler/provenance_emitter.go: token emission and signing toggle
- telemetry/pipeline/wave_aggregator.py: attribution and windowed metrics
- api/rollouts/v1/controller.go: resume/rollback endpoints and decision introspection
- console/src/components/WaveControl/ResumeGate.tsx: UI controls and manual override flow
- db/migrations/2026_02_add_provenance_index_v2.sql: migration to add provenance index and TTL policy for replay blobs

Operational considerations:
- Default sampling is 0.05% to limit replay storage growth; workspace admins can adjust sampling and retention.
- For high-TPS public customers, token signing is disabled by default but available for private clusters.
- The synchronizer runs with a leader-election guard to avoid split-brain in HA clusters.

Review highlights and responses:
- Lina Gupta: "How do we avoid cascading rollbacks when a downstream service is flapping?"
- Marcus Alvarez: "Synchronizer requires dependency health checks; if a downstream infra flaps, synchronizer will quarantine the dependent edge and escalate to human-in-the-loop instead of automatically rolling back upstream waves."

- Omar Haddad: "Retention and cost of replay blobs need clear defaults."
- Marcus Alvarez: "Set default 30 day TTL and workspace controls. Added billing note and tests for TTL eviction; storage accounted as optional add-on."

- Sofia Ruiz: "UI needs to surface rationale for resume decisions."
- Marcus Alvarez: "Console now shows gating diagnostics (which metric failed/passed and sample evidence) with links to replay samples where available."

CI summary: build and lint pass, unit/integration/e2e smoke pass.

Merge details: approved by reviewers, CI green, merge method: squash and merge. Merge message: 'Add wave synchronizer and provenance resume controller with replay support'.

Post-merge actions:
- Follow-up PR to add RBAC integration for auto-execute flag (ENG-2041).
- Add dashboards for replay storage usage and provenance ingestion (ENG-2060).

Operational playbook notes: If you observe unexpected wave state flips, check /var/log/redwood/wave-sync for leader election events, inspect decision_nonce on rollout detail, and use the replay tool to correlate sampled requests to metric spikes.

Related tickets and RFCs: ENG-1989 (synchronizer spec), ENG-2033 (provenance token design), RFC-147 (replay API).

This PR aims to reduce human toil during complex multi-wave rollouts by providing stronger attribution and safer resume semantics while keeping automation opt-in for production-critical accounts.
